Import the shared item row and sync result types in items.ts and sync.ts and delete the local duplicates.
Fall back to detection when the persisted format fails to explain a sample of the new file's dates, updating the stored value only on a successful re-detection.
Add a second audit invocation without the production-only flag, or one scoped to the relay worker, so its toolchain is covered by the same gate.
Take a pre-reconcile snapshot in syncItem before the first boundary reconcile of a run, on the same lazy pattern as the removal snapshot.
Widen the guard to scan every file under the routes and plaid folders, asserting a snapshot call precedes each destructive statement.
Re-run the prune and the periodic snapshot on a daily timer rather than only at module load.
Scope the transaction total to the live view, or add a separate archived-and-uncategorized count, so the numerator and denominator come from the same row set.
Anchor the resolution to a fixed reference such as a required statement date or the first-import date for that text, and add a test pinning the resolved date across two simulated clocks.
Consolidate the filesystem and crypto imports to the top of server.ts, then extract the remaining inline route groups into routes files to match the pattern already used for the other six.
Add a step to preship, or a job that has PowerShell available, that runs the audit-findings self-test and fails the gate on any fixture mismatch.
Log an event from the prune, snapshot and error-log-prune catch blocks in server.ts, or push the logging into the backup module itself.
Replace the per-merchant loop with one query over the full merchant list and date window, then bucket in memory the way merchantTrend already does internally.
Add a bulk uncategorize endpoint, or relax bulk categorize to accept a null category, resolving the whole list inside one database transaction.
Delete the template as superseded, or write a small publish script that pushes one canonical source into the live page so the two cannot drift again.
Pass a timeout signal on each of the four relay calls in relay.ts so a hung relay fails predictably instead of stalling the caller.
Sweep any import row still pending at boot into a failed or interrupted status, matching the pattern already used for the in-process throw case.

barRaise.reconcileNote:
Close leg, run first. Every one of the nineteen carried openFindings ids was matched against both the live queue and the archive, filtered to items tagged for this project and dated at or after the finding's first sighting. Ten came back closed, and every one of those ten carried a COMPLETELY EMPTY notes field and an empty title, so not one of them could be closed on its own record. All ten were re-verified against the code by a separate read-only pass and all ten hold: `architecture-02`, `architecture-04`, `compliance-data-steward-04`, `-05`, `-06`, `finance-product-categorization-tail-05`, `finance-product-dedupe-03`, `finance-product-threat-model-01` and `-02`, plus `finance-product-threat-model-04`, which the threat-model lens found closed by the first-launch consent modal after 15 runs open. That an entire batch of closures carried no evidence is itself worth fixing; the queue writer does not require a closure note and nothing checks for one.

`observability-03` was reported closed by nothing and is re-filed this run as `observability-01` with fresh evidence: the audit-findings self-test still is not invoked by preship, by the release script, or by the security workflow. `release-pipeline-gate-page-publish-05` stays open and moves to the deferred list rather than being reported clean, because its subject lives in another project's folder and a single-project run cannot see it, which is the same reason the previous run gave. The seven orchestration findings are carried unverified and are marked as such in the action list.
barRaise.verdictNote: Health 71 sits in the in-progress band. The verdict is one step below it on a breakage signal, not on the number: reliability-01 is live, silent, unrecoverable loss of real bank transactions on an install carrying real money.
